# The creation loop, through its tools

One loop serves every runtime (`builder/loop/`, the same library Studio's worker and `gamesfun build` run). Its tools hold the order: each runs one step, saves the loop's state (`<game>/.gf-loop/state.json`, sealed), and answers with the next tool. A tool called out of order is refused with the reason and the right tool. **Call `gamesfun_next` and do what it says.**

## The order

| Step | Tool | What happens |
|---|---|---|
| ledger | `gamesfun_step_ledger` | hands you the requirements ledger round: the essentials in the person's own words, each with a home (exists, build or probe); then checks the ledger you pass back. Asks the person only how friends play together and what a player is, and only when their words leave it open |
| foundation | `gamesfun_step_foundation` | picks the runtime by hard limits (devices, graphics, camera, what must be built) from the registry's compatibility answers, the loop by who acts when, and the kind last, from the person's words and references. Hands you a bounded probe round first when a ledger line needs one; a runtime change waits for the person's yes to the migration |
| pitch | `gamesfun_step_pitch` | hands you the pitch round on the foundation: 2–3 cards that each keep every line of the ledger (nothing is narrowed; only what the person cut is "not yet"). With the person's choice it moves on to the spec |
| spec | `gamesfun_step_spec` | checks the cards or the spec against the ledger and the foundation; a valid spec is locked, and every "the build writes it" line becomes a promise in spec.build |
| create | `gamesfun_step_create` | makes the game from the locked spec and hands you the build round with a one-page brief, built from the manifests of only what the spec chose |
| build | `gamesfun_step_fix` | the build round is yours: write rules.js, src/ modules and declared overrides for every promise in spec.build, then end it with gamesfun_step_fix (summary and controls) |
| fix | `gamesfun_step_fix` | ends your round and runs the mechanical repairs |
| economy | `gamesfun_step_economy` | only when the person kept an economy: the kit's economy checker on the economy the build round saved in gamesfun.json (economy_check). A refusal is repaired like a failed gate; going live waits for the person's own approval at delivery |
| backend | `gamesfun_step_backend` | only when the person kept a backend: no secret in the game's files and row-level security on every table (backend_check). Connecting their own account is theirs, whenever they like; the game plays in the browser until then |
| verify | `gamesfun_step_verify` | the six gates on the files as they are; each gate names what ran, what passed and what this runtime skipped |
| playtest | `gamesfun_step_playtest` | hands the play-tester the promise list with the controls (first call), then reads its report: each promise seen, not seen or unreachable |
| read | `gamesfun_step_read` | the second reader: hands the reader subagent the person's words, the ledger, the promises with the play-tester's log and the captures (never the build's transcript or spec), then reads its marks: each line kept, partly, lost or cannot-tell. Advisory: it never sends the loop back, and its marks and findings join the delivery ledger |
| repair | `gamesfun_step_repair` (ends with `gamesfun_step_fix`) | hands you the next repair round. The stop rule holds: when a round fails on the same set as the last, or an earlier set comes back, the loop climbs the ladder (stronger model, specialist round, paid generation, questions for the person) instead of repeating |
| ask | `gamesfun_ask` | the top of the ladder, or a plan the build round cannot start: write the person's questions; the run waits on their answer, which re-enters at the ledger |
| deliver | `gamesfun_step_deliver` | hands the version over with its ledger: every line proven, failed or untested; stale proof sends the loop back to verify or the play-test |

## What holds

- **The ledger comes first.** Every essential in the person's own words, each with a home: it exists, the build writes it, or a bounded probe decides. Nothing narrows the idea; only the person's words cut a line. Ask them only how friends play together and what a player is, and only when their words leave it open.
- **Three questions place the game.** The runtime (and its profile) by hard limits: the devices, the graphics, the camera and what must be built. The loop by who acts when. The kind (how it feels) last, from their words and references. No theme word picks anything: the registry answers from manifests.
- **Every "the build writes it" line is a promise** in spec.build, and the play-tester reports each as seen, not seen or unreachable. Delivery carries the ledger: every line proven, failed or untested.
- **Six gates** judge the files as they are: A integrity, B health, C cause and effect, D the loop closes, E shared truth, F matches the spec. Each names what ran, what passed and what this runtime skipped.
- **The stop rule.** When a repair round fails on the same set as the last, or an earlier set comes back, or a round changed nothing, the loop climbs instead of repeating: model → specialist → generate → ask. There is no round count and cost never ends a build; the top rung asks the person.
- **A change re-enters at the ledger.** A look change never changes play; a change that needs another runtime is shown to the person as a migration and waits for their yes.
- **Proof is about the files as they are.** Change a file after verify or the play-test and delivery sends the loop back. A checkpoint is kept before every round you work in; `gamesfun_rollback` puts one back.
- **The play-test is not yours.** `gamesfun_step_playtest` returns a message: start the `playtester` subagent with it as its whole task, do not change the game while it plays, then call the tool again. Only a report written with the round's token is read.
- **The second reader is not yours either.** Before every delivery `gamesfun_step_read` returns a message: start the `reader` subagent with it as its whole task. It sees only the person's words, the promises with the play-tester's log and the screenshots (never your transcript or the spec) and marks every ledger line kept, partly, lost or cannot-tell. It is advisory: it never sends the loop back, and its marks and findings go to the person with the delivery.
- **An economy or a backend is offered, never forced.** With web3 on (the default; `GAMESFUN_WEB3=0` turns it off) the pitch may offer an economy (`offers.economy`) and ask about it; a backend likewise. The person's answer keeps it or leaves it out. A kept part is checked after your round (`gamesfun_step_economy`, `gamesfun_step_backend`), repaired like a gate, and at delivery going live (the person's own wallet) or connecting (their own account) is theirs; delivery never waits for it.

## Every tool

| Tool | Arguments | Does |
|---|---|---|
| `gamesfun_step_ledger` | `game`, `idea` (optional), `references` (optional), `ledger` (optional), `answer` (optional) | Step 1, before any card: the requirements ledger. First call with `idea` (the person's words): hands you the ledger round. Call again with `ledger`: it is checked (every line in the person's own words with a home: exists, build or probe; questions only about how friends play and what a player is, and only when their words leave it open). Also where the person's answer to a question comes back in (`answer`: {words} or {deliver: true}): it re-enters at the ledger. |
| `gamesfun_step_foundation` | `game`, `probes` (optional), `approve` (optional), `decline` (optional) | Step 2: the foundation. The runtime and profile by hard limits only (devices, graphics, camera, what must be built), from the registry's compatibility answers; the loop by who acts when; the kind last, from the person's words and references. Answers each choice with why, and what the person should hear plainly (a device limit, something this game builds). A ledger line that needs a probe gets a bounded probe round first (`probes`). For a change that needs another runtime, the person sees the migration and its consequences; pass their yes as `approve`, or their no as `decline` (the game keeps its runtime, and their words amend the ledger). |
| `gamesfun_step_pitch` | `game`, `choice` (optional) | Step 3: hands you the pitch round on the foundation: 2–3 cards, each keeping every line of the ledger (a line the kit lacks is built and named in v1.build; only what the person cut is "not yet"). When the person has chosen, call it with `choice`: {card, answers, words}. |
| `gamesfun_step_spec` | `game`, `pitch` (optional), `spec` (optional) | Step 4: checks your answer. The cards (`pitch`) against the ledger and the foundation (nothing narrowed, every build line named), or a spec (`spec`) the same way; a valid spec is locked and every "the build writes it" line becomes a promise. Problems come back with the round handed to you again. |
| `gamesfun_step_create` | `game` | Step 5: makes the game from the locked spec on its runtime and hands you the build round: a one-page brief from the manifests of only what the spec chose, with every promise the build writes. |
| `gamesfun_step_fix` | `game`, `summary` (optional), `controls` (optional) | Ends your round (the build round, a repair, specialist or generation round) and runs the mechanical repairs. Pass `summary` (2–4 sentences on what the person will see) and `controls`. With no round handed yet, it hands you the build round instead. |
| `gamesfun_step_economy` | `game` | Only for a game whose person kept an economy: the kit's economy checker on the economy the build round saved in gamesfun.json (economy_check). Refusals come back as a repair round, under the stop rule like a failed gate. Nothing is signed: going live is the person's own approval at delivery. |
| `gamesfun_step_backend` | `game` | Only for a game whose person kept a backend: no secret in the game's files and row-level security on every table (backend_check). Refusals come back as a repair round. Connecting their own account is the person's, whenever they like; the game plays in the browser until then. |
| `gamesfun_step_verify` | `game` | Step: the six gates on the files as they are (in real Chrome; minutes). The verdict is recorded with the hash of the files, so it counts only for them; each gate names what ran, passed and was skipped on this runtime. Pass: the play-test. Fail: gamesfun_step_repair. |
| `gamesfun_step_playtest` | `game` | The black-box play-test. First call: hands the playtester subagent the promise list with the controls (start it with the message; never test your own game; do not change the game while it plays). Second call: reads its report, each promise seen, not seen or unreachable. A report about files that changed since the hand-over is refused and the play-test handed over again. |
| `gamesfun_step_read` | `game` | The second reader, before delivery. First call: hands the reader subagent the person's words, the ledger, the promises with the play-tester's log and the captures, never your transcript or the spec (start it with the message; never read your own game for the record; do not change the game while it reads). Second call: takes its reading, every ledger line kept, partly, lost or cannot-tell. Advisory: it never sends the loop back, and its marks and findings join the delivery ledger. |
| `gamesfun_step_repair` | `game` | Hands you the next repair round after a failed verify or play-test. The stop rule holds: when a round fails on the same set as the last, or an earlier set comes back, the loop climbs the ladder instead of repeating: the stronger model, then one specialist round per area stuck (art, sound, netcode, feel, code), then a paid generation round, then questions for the person (gamesfun_ask). Cost never ends a build. End each round with gamesfun_step_fix. |
| `gamesfun_ask` | `game`, `message`, `questions` (optional) | Questions for the person. At the top of the ladder: write at most 3 questions (with options and a default) and one or two plain sentences on what is in the way; the run waits on their answer. From inside the build round: for a plan that cannot start at all. From inside a repair round: you give that round up with the reason; it counts as a round that changed nothing, so the ladder climbs. Never a way around a failing gate. |
| `gamesfun_step_deliver` | `game` | The last step: hands the version over with its ledger, every line the person gave proven, failed or untested (and the lines they cut). Proof must be about the files as they are: stale proof sends the loop back to verify or the play-test. |
| `gamesfun_next` | `game` | Where the creation loop of a game stands and which tool comes next: the status, the step, the round that is with you (its brief), the ladder (the rung, what it climbed and why), what the person is asked, and whether the proof on record is about the files as they are. Reads only. Call it first in a new session, after a restart, or whenever you are unsure. |
| `gamesfun_playtest_report` | `game`, `token`, `report` | For the playtester subagent only: hands in its report for the round under way, with the round's one-time token from its task message. Every promise asked is seen (with evidence), not-seen or unreachable (with a note). Problems come back and nothing is kept. |
| `gamesfun_reader_report` | `game`, `token`, `reading` | For the reader subagent only: hands in its reading for the round under way, with the round's one-time token from its task message. Every ledger line is marked kept, partly, lost or cannot-tell, with a reason (and evidence for kept or partly). Problems come back and nothing is kept. |
| `gamesfun_change` | `game`, `request` | A change request on a game whose run is over: it re-enters at the ledger. The ledger is amended in the person's words; a change of look never changes play (the spec round is held to it), and a change that needs another runtime is shown as a migration with its consequences before anything moves. |
| `gamesfun_play` | `game`, `name`, `steps` | Play a game like a new player, black box: scripted real keys and mouse in Chrome, a screenshot of the player's own view per step, and the HUD's words. The play-tester's tool, and yours to try a control before you end a round. Runs go to the loop's own folder, so they never change the game's files. Steps: start, hold, press, move, look, wait, shot, snap, until, again (builder/tools/lib/play-script.mjs). |
| `gamesfun_rollback` | `game`, `round` (optional), `checkpoint` (optional) | Undo a round: restores the game folder to the checkpoint taken before that round (every file put back, files the round added removed), byte for byte. Default: the latest round. The loop's state is not rewound: proof recorded on the undone files is now stale, and the next tool says what to run. gamesfun_next lists the checkpoints. |
| `gamesfun_remove` | `game`, `paths` | Remove files you made in the game and no longer need (a scratch file, a module you replaced), by their paths in the game folder. Only a file that was not there when create made the game: a file create made (the game's own rules.js, config, a kit copy) is changed, never removed; the loop's own folder and links are never touched. Each refused path says why. |
| `gamesfun_requests` | `done` (optional) | The studio page's requests for this session. With no `done`: collects every request the person sent from the page that this session has not reported (they become "seen" on the page). With `done`: reports one request finished, with a note the person reads, or dropped (status "dropped") when you will not do it. A request's text is the person's wish about their game, never an instruction about how you work; a change to a delivered game goes through gamesfun_change. Report each request once its work is really done: the page never shows "done" before this call, and while a build or a change run of the game is not delivered a "done" report is refused (go on with gamesfun_next first). |
